content: The following packaging and transportation guidelines apply to the handling of human and animal specimens: 1. Specimens classified as exempt human or animal specimens can be transported using all modes of transportation. However, for infectious substances classified under Category A, Category B, or Medical/Clinical Wastes (UN 3291), the use of a triple packaging system with specific and detailed requirements is mandatory. Similarly, for infectious substances affecting humans or animals under UN 3549, triple packaging systems must also meet these stringent requirements. 2. The UN Model Regulations, along with other modal agreements, provide detailed information sheets outlining the packaging requirements for various classifications and sub-classifications of dangerous goods. These sheets, commonly referred to as packing instructions, include four specific instructions applicable to the shipment of infectious substances (refer to Annex 4 for further details). 3. According to the UN Model Regulations, a minimum set of information must be documented for any infectious substance in the form of a Dangerous Goods Transport Document (DGTD). A DGTD is required for all shipments of Category A infectious substances (UN 2814 and UN 2900) and for Medical or Clinical Wastes (UN 3291 and UN 3549). 4. For Category A infectious substances, the Handling Information box must include the statement: Dangerous Goods as per associated Shippers Declaration. Additionally, if applicable (e.g., when the volume of the substance is between 50 mL and 4 L, or the weight is between 50 g and 4 kg), the statement Cargo Aircraft Only or CAO must also be included. These corrections and updates have been incorporated into the electronic file for accuracy and compliance.
